top_findings.title: Standings double-count Brasileirao seasons 2012-2019 (Flamengo 2019: 180 pts / 76 played, true 90 / 38)
top_findings.evidence: server.py:534-540 concats data['brasileirao'] + data['historico'] then drop_duplicates(); both CSVs contain seasons 2012-2019 (380 rows each for 2019) with different team-name spellings ('Atletico-MG' vs 'Atlético-MG', 'Avai-SC' vs 'Avaí') and different column sets, so no cross-source rows dedupe. Reproduced: concat yields 760 rows for 2019; standings show Flamengo P=76 Pts=180.
top_findings.suggestion: Restrict standings to one source per season (e.g. prefer 'brasileirao' when the season exists there, else 'historico'), or dedupe on (season, round, home_team_norm, away_team_norm).

top_findings.title: Team stats (W/D/L, goals) inflated ~2x for Brasileirao 2012-2019 via duplicated all_matches
top_findings.evidence: data_loader.py:153-166 load_all_matches() concats load_brasileirao and load_historico with no cross-source dedup; get_team_stats (server.py:337-424) aggregates that frame. Reproduced: all_matches has 76 Flamengo Brasileirao-2019 rows (true 38), so every 2012-2019 Brasileirao match counts twice. Also affects search_matches counts, head-to-head, biggest wins, and average-goals denominators for those seasons.
top_findings.suggestion: Dedupe overlapping seasons in load_all_matches() on (season, round, home_team_norm, away_team_norm), or drop the historico rows for seasons >= 2012.

note: Second opinion: prior eval's R9/R6 defects CONFIRMED empirically, but reclassified missing->partial (capabilities implemented+tested; values wrong only for 2012-2019 Brasileirao overlap). Coverage 0.75 -> 0.8333.
